intro: The mask you choose depends on the age of the people wearing it and the printer you have. Simple shapes with big eye holes are easiest for children to cut, while detailed feathers and antlers need a craft knife and a steady hand. Print on heavy cardstock so the mask keeps its shape, check how much ink the design uses, and add elastic or ribbon ties after cutting. Have adults handle blades, and test the fit before decorating.

picks.description: The lion mask is the easiest animal to recognize at a glance, which makes it a good first pick for a party with mixed ages. Print it on 65-pound cardstock so the mane holds its shape, and cut the eye holes with a craft knife rather than scissors for clean edges. The mane is the largest part, so printing at letter size makes a mask that fits a child's face and a larger scaled print suits teens and adults. Add elastic cord through punched holes at the sides, and test fit before decorating. Gold and orange markers or crumpled tissue glued along the mane add texture without needing special supplies.
picks.best_for: Parties where kids want a bold, easy-to-recognize animal
picks.quirky_fact: The lion is the only big cat where males and females look clearly different, which is why the mane is the recognizable feature.
picks.shop_query: printable lion animal mask template cardstock
picks.skip_if: Very young children, since the large mane piece makes the mask top-heavy

picks.description: A watercolor fox mask has soft color edges, so it prints best on matte photo paper or lightweight cardstock with an inkjet printer. Set printing to the highest quality, and let the sheet dry for a few minutes before cutting so ink does not smear. The pointed ears can curl, so glue a thin strip of cardboard behind them. Children can also add whiskers or paint the white cheeks themselves, which makes this one a good activity for a rainy afternoon. Use a hole punch and ribbon in place of elastic if you want something softer around the ears.
picks.best_for: Craft tables where kids can paint or color the finished mask
picks.quirky_fact: Foxes use their large ears to hear small animals moving under snow or leaves.
picks.skip_if: Households without an inkjet printer, since watercolor prints can look flat on a laser
picks.product_name: Matte Photo Paper 8.5 x 11 Inkjet 50 Sheets

picks.description: The geometric owl uses angular shapes and bold outlines, so it looks good even on plain printer settings and does not need exact color matching. Because the lines are straight, it is also easy to cut accurately with a ruler and craft knife, which suits older kids and adults. Print on cardstock, score the fold lines with a ruler, and glue the layers for a slightly three-dimensional mask. Bold black outlines also let it work in black and white if you are short on ink. Use a hole punch for the side ties, and sand the eye edges lightly if the card feels rough.
picks.best_for: Older kids and adults who like clean, modern shapes
picks.quirky_fact: Owls cannot move their eyes in the socket, so they turn their heads, up to about 270 degrees.
picks.skip_if: Younger children, because the sharp angles take careful cutting
picks.product_name: Self-Healing Cutting Mat and Craft Knife Set

picks.description: The bunny mask uses pastel pinks and whites and long ears, so it is a natural fit for spring parties and Easter egg hunts. Toddlers can wear it with an elastic strap, but have an adult do the cutting. Print on cardstock and attach the ears with a small piece of tape so they stand up. Fold the inner ear pink for a bit of depth. It suits younger kids and photo ops, though the pale color can look washed out on cheap paper, so choose bright white stock for a cleaner print.
picks.best_for: Spring parties, Easter gatherings and toddlers' play
picks.quirky_fact: Rabbits can rotate their ears independently to track sounds from different directions.
picks.skip_if: Winter events, since pastel colors feel out of season
picks.product_name: Bright White Cardstock 8.5 x 11 Pastel Paper Pack

picks.description: The vintage bear mask has an earthy, hand-drawn look that fits storybook themes and rustic parties. Its brown tones print well on kraft or off-white cardstock, which gives the mask an aged look. Use a paper punch for the nose and eye holes, and sew or glue on a ribbon tie instead of elastic for a softer feel. The rounded ears are easy to cut, so it suits children from about five years old. Matte spray sealer keeps the ink from smudging on small hands, and a light coat prevents fingerprints on the dark areas.
picks.best_for: Storybook parties and cozy, low-key celebrations
picks.quirky_fact: Bears have a strong sense of smell, which scientists rank among the best of any land mammal.
picks.skip_if: Anyone who wants bright, high-contrast colors for photos
picks.product_name: Kraft Cardstock 8.5 x 11 Brown Paper 100 Sheets

picks.description: The parrot mask has saturated blues, reds and yellows, so it needs plenty of ink and looks best on glossy or heavy matte paper. Check your cartridge levels before printing a stack, and choose draft quality only if you do not mind a duller result. The curved beak is the trickiest cut, so score it lightly and fold. Add real or craft feathers for a three-dimensional effect, glued behind the edge. It suits tropical parties and summer birthdays, and adults tend to like it for photo booths because the colors show up in pictures.
picks.best_for: Summer or tropical themes and groups that like bright colors
picks.quirky_fact: Parrots are among the few animals that can copy human speech, because of their flexible tongues.
picks.skip_if: Printers low on ink, since saturated blue, red and yellow use plenty
picks.product_name: Craft Feathers Assorted Colors Parrot Mask Supplies

picks.description: The minimalist cat uses clean lines and monochrome tones, so it prints well on any printer, even in black and white, and costs little ink. It suits adults and teens at a small gathering, a costume party or a photo booth. Print on matte cardstock and cut the whisker lines with a craft knife for a delicate look. A thin elastic cord in black keeps the mask looking neat and out of the way. Because the design is plain, it also works as a base for kids to draw patterns on, and you can scale it to fit any face.
picks.best_for: Adults and teens who prefer a simple, modern look
picks.quirky_fact: Cats have about 20 whiskers on each side of the nose, used to judge gaps and movement.
picks.shop_query: printable minimalist cat mask template PDF
picks.skip_if: Children who want bright color and lots to decorate
picks.product_name: Black Elastic Cord 2 mm Round Stretch String

picks.description: The reindeer mask has antlers with holly details, so it works best for Christmas parties, school plays and photo cards taken in December. The antlers are the weak point, so print on cardstock and glue a strip of cardboard behind them. Let the antlers stand upright, and pre-bend the paper at the base. Add a red nose from a pom-pom if you like. It is quick to make, and kids can wear several during a party. Store flat in a folder, since antlers bend if left under other items, and reuse next year.
picks.best_for: Holiday parties and Christmas card photos
picks.quirky_fact: Both male and female reindeer grow antlers, unlike most deer, where only males do.
picks.skip_if: Anything outside the holiday season, since antlers and holly are Christmas-specific
picks.product_name: Red Pom Poms 1 inch Craft Pom Pom Assortment

picks.description: The panda mask has rounded black and white shapes with large simple eye patches, so it is one of the easiest to cut for younger children with supervision. Because it is mostly black and white, it prints cheaply on any printer. The eye patches use a lot of black ink in the solid areas, so use draft mode if cartridges are low. Cut the eye holes inside the patches so the mask looks natural when worn. Elastic cord through punched holes secures the mask. It suits quiet craft afternoons and class activities, and it can double as a coloring page if printed on thin paper.
picks.best_for: Younger children and groups wanting an easy mask to cut
picks.quirky_fact: Giant pandas spend up to 14 hours a day eating bamboo.
picks.skip_if: Anyone expecting lots of color, since the design is mostly black and white
picks.product_name: Kids Safety Scissors Pointed Tip 5 inch Set

picks.description: The peacock mask has teal and blue feather patterns that fan out around the eyes, so it suits costume parties, masquerade-themed evenings and adults. Fine feather details look best on glossy or heavy matte paper at high print quality. Cut the outline with a craft knife, since scissors tend to blunt the thin points. Add sequins or glitter glue at the center of each feather, and attach a thin dowel handle if you prefer a hand-held mask instead of a strap. Handle with care, as the narrow parts bend easily when stored, so keep it flat.
picks.best_for: Costume parties and adults who want a dressier, detailed mask
picks.quirky_fact: Only male peafowl have the long showy train, which they spread in display.
picks.skip_if: Young children, because the fine feather detail needs careful cutting
picks.product_name: Wooden Dowel Rods 12 inch Craft Sticks

faqs.question: What paper should I use for printable animal masks?
faqs.answer: Use 65-pound cardstock or heavier so the mask keeps its shape when worn. Matte photo paper works for detailed designs but can crease. Thin printer paper tears around the eye holes and bends in the heat of the face, so it is better for coloring pages than masks. Check that your printer accepts the thickness before loading a stack.

faqs.question: How do I attach the elastic or ribbon?
faqs.answer: Punch a hole on each side with a hole punch and thread elastic cord through, then knot it at the back. Try the mask on first to set the length. For younger children, use soft ribbon and tie it behind the head, or tape a craft stick handle to the back. Reinforce the holes with a small piece of clear tape so they do not tear.

faqs.question: Which masks are best for small children?
faqs.answer: Choose simple shapes with large eye holes, such as the panda or lion. Adults should cut the holes and handle blades, and kids can color or glue. Soft ribbon is more comfortable than elastic. Supervise small decorations such as sequins and feathers, which can be a choking risk for toddlers.

faqs.question: Can I resize a mask to fit different heads?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most printable files can be scaled in your print settings. Print one at 100 percent, hold it up, and adjust the scale up or down by 10 percent at a time until the eye holes line up. Adult faces often need a larger print than letter size, and children need slightly smaller. Keep the eye holes centered when you trim.

faqs.question: How do I store masks for next year?
faqs.answer: Keep them flat in a folder or box, since bent ears and antlers will not recover. Slip tissue paper between masks, and store away from damp and sunlight. If the elastic has stretched, replace it. Masks printed on cardstock can last several parties if kept dry.
